evals.expected_output: Autonomous-mode firing where the todo queue contains two unblocked tasks (taskId A and taskId B, both dependsOn empty/done). The routine auto-picks and executes A, completes it, then chains to and executes B within the same firing — no permission prompt, no stop after A.
expectations: start_task and complete_task are called for taskId A
the routine re-invokes /check-messages (or equivalently continues) and processes taskId B in the same firing, after taskId A
no text output asks the operator whether to continue to the second task
the firing does not stop after completing only taskId A while an unblocked taskId B remains in the todo queue

evals.expected_output: Autonomous-mode firing where check_messages returns no unread messages and list_tasks returns no unblocked todo task (queue empty). The routine produces zero text output and does not re-invoke itself.
expectations: the assistant emits zero characters of text output for this firing
the routine does not self re-invoke /check-messages after finding an empty queue
no standby block, summary, or acknowledgement word (e.g. 'court', 'ok', 'standby') is produced when queue state is unchanged from the previous firing

evals.expected_output: Autonomous-mode firing where the only todo task has an unsatisfied dependsOn (its dependency task is not status=done). The routine does not start the blocked task and stops cleanly, emitting at most a legitimate standby block if the blocked state changed since the previous firing.
expectations: mcp__vantage-peers__start_task is never called on the dependency-blocked task
no task execution output is produced for the blocked task
if the blocked-list state changed since the previous firing, output is limited to the 3-line standby block (role, instance, blocked-on list); otherwise output is zero characters
the routine does not ask the operator what to do next and does not invent alternative work
